title: Culture feature
summary: Build a responsive editorial feature with long-form copy, visual pauses, captions, and a chronology.
originNote: A recognizable editorial-design control that makes image-led atmosphere compete with sustained reading.

setup.instructions: Mount the supplied article packet, abstract map, and validator. Build a self-contained static feature page; the supplied SVG is the only image. Copy or embed every runtime input the artifact needs into the allowed published output paths; fixtures/ and validation/ are not shipped with the Dish.

turns.content: Using fixtures/article.json and fixtures/night-map.svg, build a complete responsive cultural feature as index.html. Copy the supplied SVG to assets/night-map.svg and use it in the page. Preserve every supplied paragraph, chronology entry, caption, quotation, and attribution exactly in visible, selectable text. Do not invent photography, facts, quotations, or additional reporting. Make the page inviting to wander without breaking the long reading path. Establish a clear opening hierarchy in which the title, dek, and first paragraph have distinct roles rather than equal visual volume. Include a strong opening composition, the supplied map and caption, one use of the supplied pull quote, and the complete chronology. Avoid a blog-template stack of identical cards. Use semantic article, heading, figure, caption, quotation, and time markup.

checks.description: The entry, assets/night-map.svg, and any shipped JavaScript or stylesheet assets are nonempty; JavaScript parses as modules.
At mobile and desktop widths, inspect whether the opening leads into sustained reading while the map, quote, and chronology create useful pauses.
